Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub Drivers and board code in HardFOC never call ESP-IDF or STM32Cube directly. docs.text: API guide ¶ The interfaces by task: what to call, in what order, and what to do with the result. Every block is compiled by the host build from tests/docs/ . The shape of the API ¶ Fifteen interfaces, each a header in inc/base/ , and the classes that implement them: Interface For ESP32 STM32 Host BaseAdc Analog inputs: counts and volts, averaging, multi-channel reads EspAdc StmAdc - BaseBluetooth Bluetooth / BLE: scan and connect EspBluetooth - - BaseCan CAN bus: classic and FD-sized frames, filters, bus status EspCan StmCan - BaseGpio Digital pins: direction, polarity, pulls, interrupts EspGpio StmGpio - BaseI2c One device on an I2C bus: write, read, write-then-read EspI2cDevice StmI2cDevice - BaseLogger Tagged, levelled log output EspLogger StmLogger - BaseNvs Key-value non-volatile storage: integers, strings, blobs EspNvs StmNvs HostNvs BasePeriodicTimer Periodic callback at a microsecond period EspPeriodicTimer StmPeriodicTimer - BasePio Programmable pulse I/O: symbol trains (WS2812, IR) EspPio - - BasePwm PWM channels: frequency, duty, phase EspPwm StmPwm - BaseSpi One device on an SPI bus: full-duplex transfers EspSpiDevice StmSpiDevice - BaseTemperature On-chip or external temperature sensor EspTemperature StmTemperature - BaseUart Serial port: write, read, flush, printf EspUart StmUart - BaseUsbSerialJtag USB Serial/JTAG console EspUsbSerialJtag - - BaseWifi Wi-Fi station and access point EspWifi - - Every function on this page takes the interface, so it runs on any of the platforms in the table. Initialise ¶ // Construction only stores the configuration. Initialise before the first call: most // operations return *_ERR_NOT_INITIALIZED on an object that was never initialised. bool bring_up ( BaseGpio & pin , BaseSpi & spi ) { return pin . EnsureInitialized () && spi . EnsureInitialized (); } EnsureInitialized() returns true at once when the object is already initialised, so calling it at the top of a function is cheap. Handle errors ¶ // Every interface has an error enum and a constexpr *ErrToString(). void report ( hf_spi_err_t err ) { if ( err != hf_spi_err_t :: SPI_SUCCESS ) { const auto text = HfSpiErrToString ( err ); // std::string_view std :: printf ( "SPI: %.*s \n " , static_cast < int > ( text . size ()), text . data ()); } } Compare against the success code of the interface ( SPI_SUCCESS , I2C_SUCCESS , ...). A few convenience methods return bool instead ( BaseI2c::ReadRegister() , the three-argument BaseSpi::Transfer() ); use the status-returning form when you need to know why a call failed. Drive and read pins ¶ BaseGpio works in logical states: SetActive() , SetInactive() , Toggle() and IsActive(bool&) apply the polarity given at construction ( HF_GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH or HF_GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW ), so the caller never thinks about electrical levels. SetDirection() , SetOutputMode() (push-pull or open-drain) and SetPullMode() change the configuration at run time. Interrupts are optional: ConfigureInterrupt() , EnableInterrupt() and WaitForInterrupt() return GPIO_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED on a platform without them. Talk to an I2C device ¶ A BaseI2c object is one device at one address; the bus is owned by the platform's bus class. Call Does Write(data, len, timeout_ms) One write transaction Read(data, len, timeout_ms) One read transaction WriteRead(tx, tx_len, rx, rx_len, timeout_ms) Write, repeated start, read: the usual register read WriteRegister(reg, value) / ReadRegister(reg, value) One-byte register helpers, return bool GetDeviceAddress() The device's address See the Quickstart for a complete register read. Transfer over SPI ¶ // One full-duplex transfer: chip select is driven by the device for the whole call. hf_spi_err_t read_id ( BaseSpi & spi , hf_u8_t ( & rx )[ 4 ]) { const hf_u8_t tx [ 4 ] = { 0x9F , 0x00 , 0x00 , 0x00 }; // JEDEC "read ID" return spi . Transfer ( tx , rx , sizeof ( tx ), /*timeout_ms=*/ 10 ); } Transfer() is full duplex; pass nullptr for rx to write only ( Write() ), or for tx to read only ( Read() ). TransferChain() sends several equal-length frames with a gap between them, for daisy-chained parts. Read an analog input ¶ // Average 8 samples of one channel, in volts. bool read_bus_voltage ( BaseAdc & adc , hf_channel_id_t channel , float & volts ) { return adc . ReadChannelV ( channel , volts , /*numOfSamplesToAvg=*/ 8 ) == hf_adc_err_t :: ADC_SUCCESS ; } ReadChannelCount() returns raw counts; ReadMultipleChannels() reads several channels in one call. Set a PWM duty cycle ¶ // 25 % duty on one channel; the frequency was set when the channel was configured. bool set_fan ( BasePwm & pwm , hf_channel_id_t channel ) { return pwm . EnableChannel ( channel ) == hf_pwm_err_t :: PWM_SUCCESS && pwm . SetDutyCycle ( channel , 0.25F ) == hf_pwm_err_t :: PWM_SUCCESS ; } Duty is a fraction from 0.0 to 1.0. SetDutyCycleRaw() takes timer counts; StartAll() , StopAll() and UpdateAll() act on every channel at once. Use a serial port ¶ // Write a line, then read whatever has arrived without waiting. hf_u16_t echo ( BaseUart & uart , hf_u8_t * buf , hf_u16_t size ) { const hf_u8_t hello [] = { 'h' , 'i' , '\n' }; if ( uart . Write ( hello , sizeof ( hello ), /*timeout_ms=*/ 10 ) != hf_uart_err_t :: UART_SUCCESS ) { return 0 ; } hf_u16_t n = uart . BytesAvailable (); if ( n > size ) { n = size ; } return ( n > 0U && uart . Read ( buf , n , 0 ) == hf_uart_err_t :: UART_SUCCESS ) ? n : 0U ; } Store settings ¶ // Count boots in non-volatile storage. hf_u32_t count_boot ( BaseNvs & nvs ) { hf_u32_t boots = 0 ; ( void ) nvs . GetU32 ( "boots" , boots ); // NVS_ERR_KEY_NOT_FOUND on first boot: keep 0 ++ boots ; if ( nvs . SetU32 ( "boots" , boots ) == hf_nvs_err_t :: NVS_SUCCESS ) { ( void ) nvs . Commit (); } return boots ; } SetString() / GetString() and SetBlob() / GetBlob() store text and binary values; GetMaxKeyLength() and GetMaxValueSize() give the platform limits. Commit() writes pending changes to storage. The host build has HostNvs , an in-memory implementation for tests. Run something periodically ¶ // Call a function every millisecond. The callback runs in the timer's context: keep it short. void on_tick ( void * user_data ) { auto * ticks = static_cast < hf_u32_t *> ( user_data ); ++* ticks ; } bool start_1khz ( BasePeriodicTimer & timer , hf_u32_t & ticks ) { return timer . SetCallback ( on_tick , & ticks ) == hf_timer_err_t :: TIMER_SUCCESS && timer . Start ( /*period_us=*/ 1000 ) == hf_timer_err_t :: TIMER_SUCCESS ; } GetMinPeriod() , GetMaxPeriod() and GetResolution() give the platform limits in microseconds. Send and receive CAN frames ¶ CAN has its own page: CAN . Next: CAN , or Porting to implement these interfaces on a new MCU.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ The model the library implements: abstract interfaces above, one implementation per platform below, and the rules every interface follows. Write against the interface, pick the MCU at build time Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Drivers, handlers and board HALs hold references to the abstract Base* classes (listed from inc/base/). Each platform folder under inc/mcu/ implements them with that platform's SDK: ESP32 classes over ESP-IDF, STM32 classes over STM32Cube HAL handles, and host classes for tests. The application picks one platform at build time; nothing above the interface line changes. Drawn from: inc/base/*.h Base classes ; inc/mcu/*/*.h implementations ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/interface-layers.py . Layers ¶ Layer Files Knows about Interfaces inc/base/ : BaseGpio , BaseI2c , BaseCan , ... and HardwareTypes.h C++ standard headers only ESP32 implementations inc/mcu/esp32/ , src/mcu/esp32/ ESP-IDF v5.5 drivers, FreeRTOS STM32 implementations inc/mcu/stm32/ , src/mcu/stm32/ STM32Cube HAL handles Host implementations inc/mcu/host/ C++ standard library Utilities inc/utils/ Interfaces and PlatformMutex Code above the interfaces (drivers, hf-core handlers, board HALs) includes only inc/base/ headers and holds references such as BaseSpi& . The board's start-up code is the one place that names a platform class. One call through the layers ¶ sequenceDiagram participant H as Handler (hf-core) participant B as BaseSpi participant E as EspSpiDevice participant I as ESP-IDF spi_master H->>B: Transfer(tx, rx, 4, 10) B->>E: virtual dispatch E->>E: lock, check initialised and length E->>I: spi_device_transmit() I-->>E: esp_err_t E-->>H: hf_spi_err_t::SPI_SUCCESS (statistics updated) Lifecycle ¶ Every interface follows the same three steps. Construct with a configuration. The constructor stores it and touches no hardware, so objects can be globals or members created before the scheduler starts. Initialise with EnsureInitialized() (idempotent) or Initialize() . Operations on an object that was never initialised return the interface's *_ERR_NOT_INITIALIZED . Use , and optionally Deinitialize() / EnsureDeinitialized() to release the peripheral. The interfaces are non-copyable. Platform objects that share a peripheral (several SPI or I2C devices on one bus) are created by a bus object, EspSpiBus / EspI2cBus , which owns them and returns BaseSpi* / BaseI2c* . Errors ¶ Each interface has its own enum class of error codes, defined once as an X-macro list ( HF_CAN_ERR_LIST , HF_GPIO_ERR_LIST , ...) that also generates a constexpr to-string function: Interface Error type To string BaseGpio hf_gpio_err_t HfGpioErrToString() BaseI2c hf_i2c_err_t HfI2CErrToString() BaseSpi hf_spi_err_t HfSpiErrToString() BaseCan hf_can_err_t HfCanErrToString() BaseAdc hf_adc_err_t HfAdcErrToString() BaseUart hf_uart_err_t HfUartErrToString() BaseNvs hf_nvs_err_t HfNvsErrToString() Code 0 is always success ( GPIO_SUCCESS , CAN_SUCCESS , ...). Optional features that a platform does not have return a "not supported" code ( CAN_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION , GPIO_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED , ...) from the base class default rather than failing to link. No interface throws; every method is noexcept . Statistics and diagnostics ¶ Most interfaces keep counters in the base class ( hf_can_statistics_t , hf_gpio_statistics_t , ...) and expose them through GetStatistics() / GetDiagnostics() , reset with ResetStatistics() / ResetDiagnostics() . They are for monitoring; control decisions use the return codes. Threads ¶ Platform classes guard their state with PlatformMutex ( inc/utils/PlatformMutex.h ). The mutex delegates to a backend chosen at compile time: Build Backend Effect This repository alone, host tests NullMutexBackend Every lock compiles to nothing Inside hf-core PlatformMutexBackend.h from hf-core, found with __has_include Real RTOS mutexes So a standalone build gives no locking: share an object between tasks only when a backend is configured, or serialise the calls yourself. Callbacks registered with CAN, GPIO interrupts and timers run in interrupt or timer context; keep them short and hand work to a task (for CAN, through the RX ring; see CAN ). MCU selection ¶ inc/utils/McuSelect.h turns one target macro into a family and capability macros. Under ESP-IDF it is set from CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_* ; elsewhere define exactly one HF_TARGET_MCU_* (CMake -D wins over the file). Selecting none or two is a compile error. The list is in Integration . Design choices ¶ Virtual interfaces, not templates. A board passes the same BaseGpio& to drivers in different libraries without templating them all on the platform. The cost is one indirect call per operation. No exceptions, no RTTI. The ESP-IDF component builds with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti . Buffers at set-up. The CAN RX ring and TX queue are allocated in EspCan::Initialize() , never in the interrupt that fills them. One header per interface. A driver that needs only SPI includes only BaseSpi.h and HardwareTypes.h . Next: API guide .

Optional features that a platform does not have return a "not supported" code ( CAN_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION , GPIO_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED , ...) from the base class default rather than failing to link. No interface throws; every method is noexcept .

docs.text: Most interfaces keep counters in the base class ( hf_can_statistics_t , hf_gpio_statistics_t , ...) and expose them through GetStatistics() / GetDiagnostics() , reset with ResetStatistics() / ResetDiagnostics() . They are for monitoring; control decisions use the return codes.
docs.title: Statistics and diagnostics

docs.text: Platform classes guard their state with PlatformMutex ( inc/utils/PlatformMutex.h ). The mutex delegates to a backend chosen at compile time: Build Backend Effect This repository alone, host tests NullMutexBackend Every lock compiles to nothing Inside hf-core PlatformMutexBackend.h from hf-core, found with __has_include Real RTOS mutexes So a standalone build gives no locking: share an object between tasks only when a backend is configured, or serialise the calls yourself. Callbacks registered with CAN, GPIO interrupts and timers run in interrupt or timer context; keep them short and hand work to a task (for CAN, through the RX ring; see CAN ).

docs.text: inc/utils/McuSelect.h turns one target macro into a family and capability macros. Under ESP-IDF it is set from CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_* ; elsewhere define exactly one HF_TARGET_MCU_* (CMake -D wins over the file). Selecting none or two is a compile error. The list is in Integration .
docs.title: MCU selection

docs.text: Virtual interfaces, not templates. A board passes the same BaseGpio& to drivers in different libraries without templating them all on the platform. The cost is one indirect call per operation. No exceptions, no RTTI. The ESP-IDF component builds with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti . Buffers at set-up. The CAN RX ring and TX queue are allocated in EspCan::Initialize() , never in the interrupt that fills them. One header per interface. A driver that needs only SPI includes only BaseSpi.h and HardwareTypes.h . Next: API guide .

docs.text: CAN ¶ BaseCan v2: one frame type for classic CAN and CAN FD, a send that never blocks, a receive path that works by polling, and the controller's error counters. Compiled examples from tests/docs/can.cpp . The frame ¶ hf_can_message_t carries up to 64 data bytes, so the same type serves classic CAN today and CAN FD controllers later. dlc holds the length in bytes , not the 4-bit DLC code. Field or call Meaning id 11-bit ( HF_CAN_MAX_STD_ID , 0x7FF ) or 29-bit ( HF_CAN_MAX_EXT_ID ) identifier data[64] , dlc Payload and its length in bytes: 0 to 8 classic; 0 to 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48 or 64 FD is_extended , is_rtr , is_canfd , is_brs , is_esi Frame format flags timestamp_us Receive time from the driver clock SetData(src, len) , SetLength(len) Copy or resize; return false and leave the frame unchanged if len is not valid for the frame kind SetStandardFrame() , SetExtendedFrame() , SetFdFrame(brs) , SetClassicFrame() Change the format GetDlcCode() , SetDlcCode(code) The 4-bit code, at the controller boundary Validate() , IsValid() Structural check (identifier range, length, flag combinations): an hf_can_frame_error_t GetFlags() , SetFlags() Flags packed as hf_can_flag::EXT , RTR , FDF , BRS , ESI ToFrame(out) , FromFrame(in) Convert to and from any struct with id , len , flags , data[64] , ts_us // A classic 11-bit data frame with six bytes, then the same payload as a 12-byte FD frame. bool build_frames ( hf_can_message_t & classic , hf_can_message_t & fd ) { const hf_u8_t pdo [ 6 ] = { 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 }; classic . id = 0x181 ; classic . SetStandardFrame (); if ( ! classic . SetData ( pdo , sizeof ( pdo ))) { // false: length not valid for this frame kind return false ; } fd . id = 0x181 ; fd . SetFdFrame ( /*brs=*/ true ); // FDF + bit-rate switch if ( ! fd . SetData ( pdo , sizeof ( pdo )) || ! fd . SetLength ( 12 )) { // 12 bytes: DLC code 9 return false ; } // fd.SetLength(9) would return false: 9 bytes has no FD DLC code. return classic . Validate () == hf_can_frame_error_t :: NONE && fd . IsValid (); } HfCanDlcToLen(code, fd) and HfCanLenToDlc(len, fd) convert between byte lengths and DLC codes ( HF_CAN_DLC_INVALID when a length cannot be carried). Size sizeof(hf_can_message_t) is about 104 bytes since v2 (about 40 before). Size queues and task stacks that hold frames by value accordingly. Send without blocking ¶ // Queue a frame from a control loop without ever blocking it. bool publish ( BaseCan & can , const hf_can_message_t & frame ) { switch ( can . TrySendMessage ( frame )) { // same as SendMessage(frame, 0) case hf_can_err_t :: CAN_SUCCESS : return true ; case hf_can_err_t :: CAN_ERR_QUEUE_FULL : // TX queue full: drop or retry next cycle case hf_can_err_t :: CAN_ERR_BUS_OFF : // controller is bus-off: see recover() default : return false ; } } Call Blocks Returns when TrySendMessage(msg) Never Queued, or CAN_ERR_QUEUE_FULL / CAN_ERR_BUS_OFF at once. Same as SendMessage(msg, 0) SendMessage(msg, timeout_ms) Up to timeout_ms (default 1000) Queued, or the timeout passed SendMessageBatch(msgs, n, timeout_ms) Per frame Returns how many were queued Use TrySendMessage() from control loops and protocol stacks that must not stall when the bus is busy. Receive ¶ Two delivery paths, which can be combined: Polling: ReceiveMessage(msg, timeout_ms) returns the oldest frame. With timeout_ms = 0 it returns CAN_ERR_QUEUE_EMPTY at once when nothing is waiting; otherwise it waits up to the timeout ( CAN_ERR_MESSAGE_TIMEOUT ). Callback: SetReceiveCallback(fn) calls fn for each frame, in interrupt context on ESP32. Keep it to a copy and a notification. // Drain every frame that arrived since the last call (EspCan: from the RX ring). hf_u32_t drain ( BaseCan & can , void ( * handle )( const hf_can_message_t & )) { hf_u32_t n = 0 ; hf_can_message_t m ; while ( can . ReceiveMessage ( m , /*timeout_ms=*/ 0 ) == hf_can_err_t :: CAN_SUCCESS ) { if ( m . Validate () == hf_can_frame_error_t :: NONE ) { handle ( m ); // m.GetLength() bytes are valid in m.data ++ n ; } } return n ; } On ESP32: the RX ring ¶ EspCan 's receive interrupt pushes each frame into an HfSpscRing<hf_can_message_t> , a lock-free single-producer, single-consumer ring that ReceiveMessage() drains. The interrupt never blocks or allocates; when the ring is full the new frame is dropped and counted in rx_overruns . hf_esp_can_config_t field Default Effect rx_queue_depth 32 Ring capacity, rounded up to a power of two rx_mode = AUTO yes A registered callback gets each frame; with no callback, frames go to the ring rx_mode = QUEUE_ALWAYS Every frame goes to the ring, and the callback is also called tx_queue_depth 10 Frames waiting for the controller; a full queue gives CAN_ERR_QUEUE_FULL Only one task should call ReceiveMessage() on an object at a time (or several, serialised by a mutex): the ring has one consumer. Bus status and recovery ¶ // Watch the error counters and recover from bus-off. bool recover ( BaseCan & can ) { hf_can_bus_status_t s ; if ( can . GetBusStatus ( s ) != hf_can_err_t :: CAN_SUCCESS ) { return false ; // CAN_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION on older drivers } if ( s . rx_overruns > 0U ) { // Frames were lost: the consumer is too slow or the RX ring is too small. } if ( s . state == hf_can_bus_state_t :: BUS_OFF ) { return can . RequestBusRecovery () == hf_can_err_t :: CAN_SUCCESS ; // returns at once } return s . state == hf_can_bus_state_t :: ERROR_ACTIVE ; } GetBusStatus() fills an hf_can_bus_status_t : Field Meaning state STOPPED , ERROR_ACTIVE , ERROR_WARNING , ERROR_PASSIVE or BUS_OFF tec , rec Transmit and receive error counters rx_overruns Frames lost because the RX ring was full tx_queue_full Sends refused because the TX queue was full bus_off_count Bus-off events since Initialize() The states follow ISO 11898-1 fault confinement: warning at 96, error-passive at 128, bus-off when TEC passes 255. HfCanStateFromCounters(tec, rec) gives the state the counters imply. RequestBusRecovery() starts the recovery sequence (128 occurrences of 11 recessive bits) and returns without waiting; GetBusStatus() shows ERROR_ACTIVE once the controller is back. Both return CAN_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION on an implementation that does not provide them. Filters ¶ SetAcceptanceFilter(id, mask, extended) passes frames whose identifier matches id in the bits set in mask ; ClearAcceptanceFilter() accepts everything again. Support by platform ¶ EspCan StmCan Classic CAN send and receive Yes (TWAI, ESP-IDF v5.5 node API) Yes (bxCAN or FDCAN HAL) CAN FD frames No: an FD frame returns CAN_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION FDCAN handle accepted; data-phase timing needs the FDCAN HAL extensions ReceiveMessage() polling Yes, from the RX ring Yes, blocking HAL calls TrySendMessage() Yes Yes ( SendMessage(msg, 0) ) GetBusStatus() , RequestBusRecovery() Yes Not yet: base default CAN_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION Migrating from v1 ¶ v1 v2 Action uint8_t data[8] uint8_t data[64] Code that copies sizeof(m.data) bytes into an 8-byte buffer must use m.dlc dlc was a DLC code dlc is a length in bytes No change for classic frames; FD code that stored a code (9 to 15) stores the length or calls SetDlcCode() canfd_dlc removed Use dlc SetDLC(len) accepted 0 to 64 on FD frames exact FD lengths only, 0 to 8 on classic Check the bool result EspCan::ReceiveMessage() always unsupported returns frames Polling loops start receiving; with a callback, set rx_mode = QUEUE_ALWAYS to get both EspCan::SendMessage() slept after each frame no sleep Callers that relied on the pacing must pace themselves Next: ESP32 , or hf-core 's CANopen utilities, which run over BaseCan .

docs.text: Integration ¶ How to add the library to a build: ESP-IDF component, the host test build, include paths and the configuration macros. As a git submodule ¶ git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-internal-interface-wrap.git components/hf-internal-interface-wrap Inside the HardFOC stack you do not add it yourself: hf-core-drivers carries it as internal/hf-internal-interface-wrap , and hf-core brings in hf-core-drivers. ESP-IDF component ¶ The root CMakeLists.txt registers an ESP-IDF component with every source in src/mcu/esp32/ and src/utils/ . Point the project at the folder: CMakeLists.txt (project) cmake_minimum_required ( VERSION 3.16 ) set ( EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS components/hf-internal-interface-wrap ) include ( $ENV{ IDF_PATH } /tools/cmake/project.cmake ) project ( my_app ) and list the component in main/CMakeLists.txt ( REQUIRES hf-internal-interface-wrap ; the component name is the folder name). Setting Value Include directories inc , inc/base , inc/mcu/esp32 , inc/mcu/esp32/utils , inc/utils Language C++20 ( cxx_std_20 ), -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti Public requirements freertos , esp_common , esp_hw_support , esp_system , log , soc , hal , esp_wifi , bt , nvs_flash , esp_driver_i2c , and esp_driver_usb_serial_jtag when ESP-IDF has it Private requirements esp_netif , esp_event , esp_timer , lwip Both include styles work: #include "BaseGpio.h" and #include "base/BaseGpio.h" , #include "EspGpio.h" and #include "mcu/esp32/EspGpio.h" . Other build systems ¶ Code that only uses the interfaces needs nothing but the headers: add inc , inc/base and inc/utils to the include path. That is how the host tests build ( tests/host/CMakeLists.txt ). A platform's sources are added by that platform's build; this repository has no CMake target for the STM32 sources. MCU selection ¶ inc/utils/McuSelect.h needs exactly one target. Under ESP-IDF it comes from CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_* ; elsewhere pass it on the command line ( -DHF_TARGET_MCU_STM32H7 ) or uncomment it in the file. Macro Family HF_MCU_NAME HF_TARGET_MCU_ESP32C6 HF_MCU_FAMILY_ESP32 ESP32-C6 HF_TARGET_MCU_ESP32 HF_MCU_FAMILY_ESP32 ESP32 HF_TARGET_MCU_ESP32S2 HF_MCU_FAMILY_ESP32 ESP32-S2 HF_TARGET_MCU_ESP32S3 HF_MCU_FAMILY_ESP32 ESP32-S3 HF_TARGET_MCU_ESP32C3 HF_MCU_FAMILY_ESP32 ESP32-C3 HF_TARGET_MCU_ESP32C2 HF_MCU_FAMILY_ESP32 ESP32-C2 HF_TARGET_MCU_ESP32H2 HF_MCU_FAMILY_ESP32 ESP32-H2 HF_TARGET_MCU_STM32F4 HF_MCU_FAMILY_STM32 STM32F4 HF_TARGET_MCU_STM32H7 HF_MCU_FAMILY_STM32 STM32H7 HF_TARGET_MCU_RP2040 HF_MCU_FAMILY_RP2040 RP2040 HF_TARGET_MCU_NONE HF_MCU_FAMILY_NONE None (software-only) Headers that need it ( HfTime.h , the ESP32 type headers) include it themselves; the Base* headers do not, so code that uses only the interfaces builds without a target. Configuration macros ¶ Macro Default Effect HF_TARGET_MCU_* from ESP-IDF, else none (compile error) Selects the platform HF_THREAD_SAFE defined in McuSelect.h Reserved: no code tests it today; locking comes from PlatformMutex PLATFORM_MUTEX_BACKEND_CONFIGURED set by a PlatformMutexBackend.h on the include path PlatformMutex uses a real RTOS backend instead of no-ops Next: Testing and CI .

docs.text: Porting ¶ How to bring the interfaces to a new MCU: what to implement, in what order, and how to check it. What a port is ¶ A port is a folder inc/mcu/<platform>/ plus src/mcu/<platform>/ with one class per interface you need. Each class derives from a Base* class and implements its pure virtual methods with the vendor SDK. Nothing in inc/base/ or in the code above it changes. Start with the interfaces your board's drivers use (usually GPIO, SPI, I2C, UART, then CAN, ADC, PWM and a timer), not all fifteen. The methods to implement ¶ Interface Methods a port must implement BaseAdc (7) Initialize() , Deinitialize() , GetMaxChannels() , IsChannelAvailable() , ReadChannelV() , ReadChannelCount() , ReadChannel() BaseBluetooth (45) Initialize() , Deinitialize() , IsInitialized() , Enable() , Disable() , IsEnabled() , SetMode() , GetMode() , GetLocalAddress() , SetDeviceName() , GetDeviceName() , ConfigureClassic() , SetDiscoverable() , IsDiscoverable() , ConfigureBle() , StartAdvertising() , StopAdvertising() , IsAdvertising() , StartScan() , StopScan() , IsScanning() , GetDiscoveredDevices() , ClearDiscoveredDevices() , Connect() , Disconnect() , IsConnected() , GetConnectedDevices() , Pair() , Unpair() , IsPaired() , GetPairedDevices() , SendData() , GetAvailableData() , ReadData() , DiscoverServices() , DiscoverCharacteristics() , ReadCharacteristic() , WriteCharacteristic() , SubscribeCharacteristic() , GetState() , GetRssi() , RegisterEventCallback() , UnregisterEventCallback() , RegisterDataCallback() , UnregisterDataCallback() BaseCan (8) Initialize() , Deinitialize() , SendMessage() , ReceiveMessage() , SetReceiveCallback() , SetAcceptanceFilter() , GetStatus() , Reset() BaseGpio (12) SetDirectionImpl() , GetDirectionImpl() , SetOutputModeImpl() , GetOutputModeImpl() , SetPullModeImpl() , GetPullModeImpl() , SetPinLevelImpl() , GetPinLevelImpl() , IsPinAvailable() , GetMaxPins() , GetDescription() , Initialize() BaseI2c (6) Initialize() , Deinitialize() , Write() , Read() , WriteRead() , GetDeviceAddress() BaseLogger (26) Initialize() , Deinitialize() , IsInitialized() , EnsureInitialized() , SetLogLevel() , GetLogLevel() , Error() , Warn() , Info() , Debug() , Verbose() , Log() , LogV() , LogWithLocation() , Flush() , IsLevelEnabled() , GetStatistics() , GetDiagnostics() , ResetStatistics() , ResetDiagnostics() , IsHealthy() , GetLastError() , GetLastErrorMessage() , PrintStatistics() , PrintDiagnostics() , PrintStatus() BaseNvs (15) Initialize() , Deinitialize() , SetU32() , GetU32() , SetString() , GetString() , SetBlob() , GetBlob() , EraseKey() , Commit() , KeyExists() , GetSize() , GetDescription() , GetMaxKeyLength() , GetMaxValueSize() BasePeriodicTimer (12) Initialize() , Deinitialize() , Start() , Stop() , SetPeriod() , GetPeriod() , GetStats() , ResetStats() , GetDescription() , GetMaxPeriod() , GetMinPeriod() , GetResolution() BasePio (14) Initialize() , Deinitialize() , ConfigureChannel() , Transmit() , StartReceive() , StopReceive() , IsChannelBusy() , GetChannelStatus() , GetCapabilities() , SetTransmitCallback() , SetReceiveCallback() , SetErrorCallback() , ClearChannelCallbacks() , ClearCallbacks() BasePwm (15) Initialize() , Deinitialize() , EnableChannel() , DisableChannel() , IsChannelEnabled() , SetDutyCycle() , SetDutyCycleRaw() , SetFrequency() , SetPhaseShift() , StartAll() , StopAll() , UpdateAll() , SetComplementaryOutput() , GetDutyCycle() , GetFrequency() BaseSpi (4) Initialize() , Deinitialize() , Transfer() , GetDeviceConfig() BaseTemperature (5) Initialize() , Deinitialize() , ReadTemperatureCelsiusImpl() , GetSensorInfo() , GetCapabilities() BaseUart (8) Initialize() , Deinitialize() , Write() , Read() , BytesAvailable() , FlushTx() , FlushRx() , Printf() BaseUsbSerialJtag (6) Initialize() , Deinitialize() , Write() , Read() , FlushTx() , IsHostConnected() BaseWifi (30) Initialize() , Deinitialize() , IsInitialized() , SetMode() , GetMode() , ConfigureStation() , Connect() , Disconnect() , IsConnected() , GetRssi() , GetIpInfo() , ConfigureAccessPoint() , StartAccessPoint() , StopAccessPoint() , IsAccessPointActive() , GetConnectedStationCount() , StartScan() , GetScanResults() , IsScanning() , GetState() , GetConnectedSsid() , GetConnectedBssid() , SetPowerSave() , GetPowerSave() , RegisterEventCallback() , UnregisterEventCallback() , GetMacAddress() , SetMacAddress() , GetChannel() , SetChannel() Everything else in an interface has a working default in the base class: lazy initialisation, polarity handling, statistics, batch helpers, and "not supported" returns for optional features. Override those only to do better (for example, a hardware TransferChain() for SPI, or GetBusStatus() for CAN). A complete GPIO port ¶ The smallest complete implementation, compiled by the host build from tests/docs/port_gpio.cpp . BaseGpio turns SetActive() into SetPinLevelImpl(HIGH) or LOW depending on the polarity, and validates the object before calling the port. #include "BaseGpio.h" // A GPIO for a new MCU. BaseGpio does the polarity, validation and statistics; // the port only moves the pin. class MyMcuGpio : public BaseGpio { public : explicit MyMcuGpio ( hf_pin_num_t pin , hf_gpio_direction_t dir = hf_gpio_direction_t :: HF_GPIO_DIRECTION_OUTPUT , hf_gpio_active_state_t active = hf_gpio_active_state_t :: HF_GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH ) noexcept : BaseGpio ( pin , dir , active ) {} bool Initialize () noexcept override { // Configure the pin's mux, direction and pulls with the vendor SDK. return SetDirectionImpl ( current_direction_ ) == hf_gpio_err_t :: GPIO_SUCCESS ; } bool IsPinAvailable () const noexcept override { return pin_ >= 0 && pin_ < GetMaxPins (); } hf_u8_t GetMaxPins () const noexcept override { return 32 ; // pins on this MCU } const char * GetDescription () const noexcept override { return "MyMcu GPIO" ; } protected : hf_gpio_err_t SetDirectionImpl ( hf_gpio_direction_t d ) noexcept override { direction_ = d ; return hf_gpio_err_t :: GPIO_SUCCESS ; } hf_gpio_err_t GetDirectionImpl ( hf_gpio_direction_t & d ) const noexcept override { d = direction_ ; return hf_gpio_err_t :: GPIO_SUCCESS ; } hf_gpio_err_t SetOutputModeImpl ( hf_gpio_output_mode_t m ) noexcept override { mode_ = m ; return hf_gpio_err_t :: GPIO_SUCCESS ; } hf_gpio_err_t GetOutputModeImpl ( hf_gpio_output_mode_t & m ) const noexcept override { m = mode_ ; return hf_gpio_err_t :: GPIO_SUCCESS ; } hf_gpio_err_t SetPullModeImpl ( hf_gpio_pull_mode_t p ) noexcept override { pull_ = p ; return hf_gpio_err_t :: GPIO_SUCCESS ; } hf_gpio_pull_mode_t GetPullModeImpl () const noexcept override { return pull_ ; } hf_gpio_err_t SetPinLevelImpl ( hf_gpio_level_t level ) noexcept override { level_ = level ; // write the output data register here return hf_gpio_err_t :: GPIO_SUCCESS ; } hf_gpio_err_t GetPinLevelImpl ( hf_gpio_level_t & level ) noexcept override { level = level_ ; // read the input data register here return hf_gpio_err_t :: GPIO_SUCCESS ; } private : hf_gpio_direction_t direction_ { hf_gpio_direction_t :: HF_GPIO_DIRECTION_INPUT }; hf_gpio_output_mode_t mode_ { hf_gpio_output_mode_t :: HF_GPIO_OUTPUT_MODE_PUSH_PULL }; hf_gpio_pull_mode_t pull_ { hf_gpio_pull_mode_t :: HF_GPIO_PULL_MODE_FLOATING }; hf_gpio_level_t level_ { hf_gpio_level_t :: HF_GPIO_LEVEL_LOW }; }; Rules for an implementation ¶ Rule Why Constructors store configuration only; Initialize() touches hardware and sets initialized_ Objects are created as globals and members before the scheduler runs Return the interface's error codes, never vendor codes Callers compare against *_SUCCESS and the *_ERR_* list Every method is noexcept ; no exceptions, no RTTI The component builds with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti Allocate in Initialize() , never in an interrupt Interrupt handlers must not block or allocate Guard shared state with PlatformMutex It becomes a real mutex when a backend is configured (see Architecture ) Callbacks from interrupts get copies, not pointers into driver buffers The buffer may be reused before the callback's work runs timeout_ms = 0 means "do not wait" BaseCan::TrySendMessage() and polling receives rely on it Wire it into the build ¶ Add HF_TARGET_MCU_<NAME> and its family block to inc/utils/McuSelect.h . Add a monotonic time source inc/mcu/<platform>/<X>Time.h and its #elif in inc/utils/HfTime.h . Add a PlatformMutexBackend.h for the platform's RTOS where the stack is assembled (hf-core does this for FreeRTOS). Build the sources with the platform's toolchain; the ESP-IDF component in the root CMakeLists.txt is the model. Check a port ¶ Check How It compiles against the interface Instantiate every class once, as port_gpio.cpp does; an unimplemented pure virtual is a compile error Lifecycle Call each method before Initialize() (expect *_ERR_NOT_INITIALIZED ), then after Polarity An active-low BaseGpio : SetActive() must drive the pin low CAN Loopback mode, then TrySendMessage() until CAN_ERR_QUEUE_FULL , then GetBusStatus() On hardware Port the matching ESP32 test application from examples/esp32/main The ESP32 classes are the reference implementation; the STM32 classes show the CubeMX-handle style. Next: Utilities .

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Write one function against the interfaces, then give it ESP32 objects: an LED pin and an I2C sensor. 1. Add the component ¶ Clone the repository into your ESP-IDF project and list it as an extra component directory (details in Integration ): git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-internal-interface-wrap.git components/hf-internal-interface-wrap The component needs ESP-IDF v5.5 or later (the TWAI node API that EspCan uses) and C++20. 2. Write portable code ¶ The function below takes the interfaces, not ESP32 classes, so it builds unchanged for STM32 or a host test. It is compiled by the host build from tests/docs/quickstart.cpp . #include "BaseGpio.h" #include "BaseI2c.h" // Reads a sensor's WHO_AM_I register and lights an LED when it matches. // Nothing here knows which MCU it runs on: pass in EspGpio / EspI2cDevice, // StmGpio / StmI2cDevice, or a test double. bool check_sensor ( BaseI2c & sensor , BaseGpio & led ) { constexpr hf_u8_t kWhoAmIReg = 0x0F ; constexpr hf_u8_t kExpectedId = 0x6C ; if ( ! sensor . EnsureInitialized () || ! led . EnsureInitialized ()) { return false ; // configures the device and the pin; a no-op the second time } hf_u8_t id = 0 ; if ( ! sensor . ReadRegister ( kWhoAmIReg , id )) { // write the register address, read one byte return false ; // no ACK: wiring, address or pull-ups } const bool ok = ( id == kExpectedId ); const hf_gpio_err_t err = ok ? led . SetActive () : led . SetInactive (); // polarity-aware return ok && err == hf_gpio_err_t :: GPIO_SUCCESS ; } 3. Create the ESP32 objects ¶ main.cpp #include "mcu/esp32/EspGpio.h" #include "mcu/esp32/EspI2c.h" extern "C" void app_main () { EspGpio led ( 8 , hf_gpio_direction_t :: HF_GPIO_DIRECTION_OUTPUT ); // GPIO8, active high hf_i2c_master_bus_config_t bus_cfg ; // I2C_NUM_0, internal pull-ups bus_cfg . sda_io_num = 6 ; bus_cfg . scl_io_num = 7 ; EspI2cBus bus ( bus_cfg ); if ( ! bus . Initialize ()) { return ; // pins or port already in use } hf_i2c_device_config_t dev_cfg ; dev_cfg . device_address = 0x6A ; // 7-bit address dev_cfg . scl_speed_hz = 400000 ; BaseI2c * sensor = bus . GetDevice ( bus . CreateDevice ( dev_cfg )); if ( sensor == nullptr || ! check_sensor ( * sensor , led )) { // wrong address, no pull-ups, or the sensor did not answer } } Construction only stores the configuration. The bus is set up by bus.Initialize() , which must come before CreateDevice() ; the pin and the device are set up by the EnsureInitialized() calls in check_sensor() . What each step does ¶ Step What happens EspGpio led(...) Stores pin, direction and polarity. No register is written yet EspI2cBus bus(cfg) Stores the bus settings: port, pins, glitch filter, pull-ups bus.Initialize() Creates the ESP-IDF I2C master bus CreateDevice(dev_cfg) Adds a device at that address and speed and returns its index, or -1 (bus not initialised, address in use) GetDevice(index) Returns the device as a BaseI2c* ( nullptr for a bad index) EnsureInitialized() Configures the pin, adds the device to the ESP-IDF bus; does nothing the second time ReadRegister(reg, id) WriteRead() of one address byte and one data byte SetActive() Drives the pin to its active level (high here, low for an active-low pin) If it does not work ¶ Symptom Check CreateDevice() returns -1 bus.Initialize() was not called or failed, or the address is already on the bus ReadRegister() returns false The 7-bit address (not shifted), SDA / SCL pins swapped, external pull-ups on a long bus The LED never lights The pin number and HF_GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW for an LED wired to 3.3 V Link errors for Esp* symbols The component directory is not in EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS #error "No MCU selected!" A non-ESP-IDF build must define one HF_TARGET_MCU_* (see Integration ) Next: Architecture , or the API guide for the other interfaces.

docs.text: STM32 ¶ The state of the STM32 implementations: what exists, how they are meant to be used, and what is not done yet. Early The STM32 classes are not built or tested by this repository's CI, there is no CMake target for them here, and they have not been run on hardware as part of this repository. Treat them as a starting point for a port, not a finished platform. What exists ¶ Eleven interfaces have an STM32 class under inc/mcu/stm32/ and src/mcu/stm32/ : Interface STM32 class BaseAdc StmAdc BaseCan StmCan (bxCAN or FDCAN handle) BaseGpio StmGpio BaseI2c StmI2cDevice BaseLogger StmLogger BaseNvs StmNvs (with StmNvsBackend ) BasePeriodicTimer StmPeriodicTimer BasePwm StmPwm BaseSpi StmSpiDevice BaseTemperature StmTemperature BaseUart StmUart There is no STM32 class for Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, PIO or USB Serial/JTAG. How they are used ¶ The classes wrap the handles STM32CubeMX generates; they do not configure clocks, pins or peripherals themselves. Initialise the peripheral with the generated MX_*_Init() code, then pass the handle: extern ADC_HandleTypeDef hadc1 ; // from CubeMX extern CAN_HandleTypeDef hcan1 ; StmAdc adc ( & hadc1 ); StmCan can ( & hcan1 ); // or StmCan(&hfdcan1) for FDCAN Select the family with HF_TARGET_MCU_STM32F4 or HF_TARGET_MCU_STM32H7 (see Integration ). Not done yet ¶ Gap Effect StmCan has no GetBusStatus() / RequestBusRecovery() Both return CAN_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION (base default) CAN FD data-phase timing Needs the FDCAN HAL extensions No build or test in CI Changes to inc/base/ can break the STM32 classes unnoticed HfTime.h includes Stm32Time.h , which does not exist yet hf_time::MonotonicUs() does not build for an STM32 target No STM32 example application Nothing to flash for a first check The porting plan for running the whole HardFOC stack on an STM32H7 is in hf-core ( STM32H7_PORTING.md ). Next: Porting .

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the library is checked: host unit tests, compiled documentation, ESP32 builds and static analysis, on every pull request. Host unit tests ¶ The host tests build the MCU-independent code with GCC or Clang, warnings as errors, and run it without hardware. cmake -S tests/host -B build/host -G Ninja cmake --build build/host ctest --test-dir build/host --output-on-failure File Covers tests/host/test_can_frame.cpp hf_can_message_t (BaseCan v2): lengths, DLC codes, flags, validation, conversion to the transport-neutral frame layout tests/host/test_spsc_ring.cpp HfSpscRing : capacity rounding, full and empty, overruns, counter wrap, a producer and a consumer thread tests/host/HostTest.h The minimal test framework -DHF_HOST_SANITIZE=address adds AddressSanitizer and UBSan; -DHF_HOST_SANITIZE=thread adds ThreadSanitizer, which the ring's two-thread test is written for. Documentation snippets ¶ Every multi-line C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target hf_iiw_doc_snippets ) with the same warnings. A change to an interface that breaks a page breaks the build first. The README's example is a copy of the Quickstart snippet that hardfoc-docs gen --check keeps in step. docs.text: Utilities ¶ Helpers in inc/utils/ for code that uses the interfaces: what each one is for, how to use it and what it costs. Header What it is DigitalOutputGuard.h RAII: a BaseGpio is active while the guard lives SoftChipSelectGuard.h RAII: a software chip select asserted for one SPI frame HfSpscRing.h Lock-free single-producer, single-consumer ring for ISR-to-task hand-off PlatformMutex.h Mutex, shared mutex and lock guards with a compile-time backend HfTime.h Monotonic microsecond clock, selected per MCU McuSelect.h Target MCU, family and capability macros memory_utils.h make_unique_nothrow<T>() : allocation that returns nullptr instead of throwing AsciiArtGenerator.h Text banners for test output DigitalOutputGuard ¶ Sets a pin to output and active on construction, inactive on destruction, including every early return. Use it for an enable line that must drop when a function exits. hf_gpio_err_t test_with_driver_enabled ( BaseGpio & driver_enable_pin ) { DigitalOutputGuard enable ( driver_enable_pin ); // output + active if ( ! enable . IsValid ()) { return enable . GetLastError (); } run_motor_test (); return hf_gpio_err_t :: GPIO_SUCCESS ; } // inactive here, on every return path Cost: a SetDirection() (when ensure_output_mode is true), a SetActive() and a SetInactive() ; no allocation. SoftChipSelectGuard ¶ Runs an assert callable on construction and a deassert callable on destruction; Release() deasserts early. It only owns the chip-select edges: hold the bus lock for the whole frame yourself. void one_frame ( BaseGpio & cs_pin ) { SoftChipSelectGuard cs {[ & ] { ( void ) cs_pin . SetActive (); }, [ & ] { ( void ) cs_pin . SetInactive (); }}; // the SPI frame goes here; the caller already holds the bus lock } // chip select released here Cost: the two callables, inlined; no allocation. HfSpscRing ¶ One producer (usually an interrupt) calls TryPush() , one consumer calls TryPop() ; neither blocks, locks or allocates. Init(n) allocates the storage once, rounded up to a power of two (at most kMaxCapacity , 65536). A push into a full ring drops the new element and counts it in Overruns() . EspCan uses it for received frames. Cost: n elements of storage; each push or pop is two atomic loads and one atomic store. PlatformMutex ¶ PlatformMutex , PlatformSharedMutex , PlatformUniqueLock and PlatformSharedLock mirror the standard library types. With no backend they compile to nothing; with a PlatformMutexBackend.h on the include path they use the RTOS (see Architecture ). HfTime ¶ hf_time::MonotonicUs() reads the platform's microsecond counter ( esp_timer on ESP32), inlined, without a virtual call. MonotonicMs() and ElapsedUs(t0) are built on it. Under HF_TARGET_MCU_NONE it returns 0; tests that need time inject their own clock. Next: Examples .
